text:
WOLFPEN COUNTY SCHOOLS - OFFICE OF SPECIAL EDUCATION
ELIGIBILITY DETERMINATION / INITIAL ARC CONFERENCE SUMMARY
Disability Under Consideration: TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY
Authority: 707 KAR 1:310; 34 CFR 300.8(c)(12)
Ref. No.: WCS-TBI-2627-008                               Page 1 of 3

STUDENT: VANHOOSE, BRIER NICOLE         DOB: 11/03/2013    Age: 12-10
Grade: 7     Student #: 450118273     KY Medicaid: 7718840236
School: Wolfpen Middle School (WMS), Team 7-Gold, Rm 208
Parents: Rhea Vanhoose (mother), Jody Vanhoose (father)
Physical: 812 Puncheon Creek Rd., Frogtown community
Mailing: P.O. Box 61, Kelsa, KY 41659
Phone: home 555-0134 (landline); mother cell (606) 555-0157;
       father (work) 606.555.0189
Email: rhea.vanhoose@example.com
Case manager: dburchett@wolfpen.example.org, 606-555-0110 ext. 2204
Referral: 08/24/2026   Consent to evaluate: 8-28-26   ARC: October 2, 2026, 3:30 PM, WMS library

REASON FOR REFERRAL
Brier Nicole Vanhoose ("Bri") was a typical learner through 6th grade with no prior referrals or retentions. On June 14 she was a passenger when her papaw's side-by-side rolled on the ridge road above the old strip job. She was flown to Bluestone Regional Medical Center (MRN BRMC-00761435) with a left frontal contusion and diffuse axonal injury, spent 11 days in the PICU, then completed inpatient rehab at Ashford Children's Rehabilitation Hospital and was discharged 7-2-26. Kentucky State Police collision report 2026-114-0388 is in the confidential file. Mrs. Vanhoose made a written referral to Mrs. Burchett the first week of the 2026-27 school year.

HEALTH (reviewed by school nurse Nikki Dotson, RN)
- One post-traumatic seizure 7/19; now on Keppra 500 mg twice daily. Seizure action plan on file.
- Left-sided weakness; wears a left AFO. Outpatient PT twice weekly at Puncheon Creek Family Clinic.
- Daily headaches and light sensitivity; fatigue by 1:00 PM most days.
- Vision and hearing screenings PASSED 9/4/26.
- Neuropsychological evaluation by Dr. Mei-Lin Castellano, Ph.D., Ashford Children's (859-555-0146); report received on 9/24.

EVALUATION DATA
Administered the week of 9/15 by Nolan Stepp, Ed.S., NCSP, school psychologist.
Measure                           Score      %ile   Range
WISC-V Verbal Comprehension       VCI 96     39     Average
WISC-V Visual Spatial             VSI 81     10     Low Average
WISC-V Fluid Reasoning            FRI 86     18     Low Average
WISC-V Working Memory             WMI 74     4      Very Low
WISC-V Processing Speed           PSI 64     1      Extremely Low
WIAT-4 Reading Comprehension      SS 91      27     Average
WIAT-4 Math Problem Solving       SS 80      9      Low Average
WIAT-4 Essay Composition          SS 77      6      Very Low
NEPSY-II Inhibition-Switching     ss 4       2      Well Below Expected
BRIEF-2 Teacher Working Memory    T = 79     --     Clinically Elevated

Before the injury Brier scored Proficient in reading and Apprentice in math on the grade 6 KSA. She now reads at a 6th-grade level on the district benchmark but needs text re-read aloud to answer 2-step questions. With a reduced load she completes 3/4 of in-class math assignments, and 1/4 without it; she retains 2 of 5 new vocabulary terms after 24 hours. Student interview (B.N.V., 9/17): she says math "goes blank" and the hallway noise "hurts."

TEACHER AND PARENT INPUT
Mrs. Joanie Cantrell (7th grade ELA): Brier is kind and works hard, but loses her place after about 15 minutes and asks for the nurse by 6th period.
Coach Darnell Wooten: she was the only girl on the WMS wrestling team last season.
Mother: Bri sleeps 11-12 hours, is short-fused with her sister Kinley, and cries when she can't remember assignments. The family moved back from Indiana in 2016 when Jody took a job driving log truck for Hatcher Lumber Co. in Kelsa. Brier sings specials at Frogtown Holiness Church and misses Wednesday night service when headaches flare. Papaw Orville Vanhoose drives her to PT on Tuesdays and "has not been right since the wreck."

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA (707 KAR 1:310)
[X] Acquired injury to the brain caused by external physical force (medical documentation, Dr. Harold Ashby, neurosurgery)
[X] Impairment in cognition, memory, attention, problem-solving, motor and physical functions, and information processing
[X] Adverse effect on educational performance (PSI 64, WMI 74, Essay Composition SS 77, work completion)
[X] Not congenital, degenerative, or induced by birth trauma
[X] Needs specially designed instruction
DETERMINATION: ELIGIBLE - Traumatic Brain Injury (primary). The ARC considered Other Health Impairment; not selected.

ARC DECISIONS
1. IEP developed today. LRE: general education 80% or more of the day.
2. Services                                         Frequency
   SDI Math (collaborative)                          50 min/day, 5 days/wk
   SDI Written Expression (resource)                 30 min/day, 3 days/wk
   Speech/Language - cognitive-communication         30 min x 2/wk (Tatum Rowland, CCC-SLP)
   OT consultation                                   30 min/month (L. Crase, OTR/L)
   School health services (seizure plan, headaches)  as needed
3. Accommodations: rest break every 20 minutes; reduced workload (fewer items, same skill); extended time 1.5x; elevator pass and early class release; reduced-glare seating; adapted PE.
4. Return-to-learn plan reviewed with Dr. Ashby's office. The ARC will reconvene 10/29/26, or sooner if medical status changes.

SAMPLE GOALS
- Given a planner checklist and one adult prompt, Brier will record all assignments before leaving each class in 4 of 5 trials across 3 consecutive weeks.
- Using a 4-part organizer, Brier will write a paragraph scoring 3 of 4 on the district writing rubric.

title: Manifestation Determination Review - OHI (ADHD), Grade 9, Bus-Line Incident (fictional test record)
text:
KINNARD COUNTY PUBLIC SCHOOLS
MANIFESTATION DETERMINATION REVIEW (MDR) - ARC CONFERENCE RECORD
Authority: 34 CFR 300.530(e); 707 KAR 1:340
MDR No.: KCS-MDR-26-0031        Discipline Ref.: DR-26-04471        Pg 1 of 2

STUDENT: KILGORE-ESTEP, RYDER J.      DOB: 2-7-12     Grade: 9     SSID: 8830412967
School: North Kinnard High School (NKHS)          Bus: 31
Eligibility: Other Health Impairment (ADHD, combined presentation)
Current IEP: 3/3/26     BIP last revised: 3/3/26     Case manager: Ms. Alana Presley
Parent: Misty Kilgore (mother)
Address: 4020 Pawpaw Branch Rd. / HC 71 Box 1540, Sabra, KY 41736
Phone: 606-555-0161 (cell); work 555-0129 ext. 12     Email: misty.kilgore88@example.com
School contact: (606) 555-0140 x3301, apresley@kinnard.example.org

Incident date: 09/15/2026, approx. 7:52 AM, bus loading zone
Removal: out-of-school suspension 9/16 through 9/25/26 (8 school days), with a recommendation for an expulsion hearing - a proposed change of placement
MDR held: September 23, 2026, 1:15 PM, NKHS conference room, within 10 school days of the decision to change placement

ATTENDEES                  ROLE                                   PRESENT
Mrs. Glenna Mosley         DoSE / Chair                           Y
Misty Kilgore              Parent                                 Y
Wilma Thacker              Parent advocate (invited by parent)    Y
Ryder                      Student (first 15 minutes)             Y
Ms. Alana Presley          Sp Ed Teacher / Case Manager           Y
Mr. Wes Kirby              Gen Ed Teacher (Algebra I)             Y
Dr. Sonya Belcher          School Psychologist                    Y
Mr. Curtis Hammonds        Assistant Principal                    Y
Ms. Kiara Vance            School Counselor                       Y (video)

INCIDENT SUMMARY
From Mr. Hammonds' incident report and the statement of SRO Deputy Trent Maynard: Ryder James Kilgore-Estep was waiting in line for Bus 31 when a peer (Student B) made comments about Ryder's father being "in the pen." Ryder shoved Student B into the rail and struck him twice; Student B had a split lip and was seen by the nurse. Ryder then ran toward the ag barn and was found by Mr. Hammonds about 20 minutes later. Deputy Maynard filed a juvenile complaint (CDW-26-1187) with the court designated worker. Bus driver Luther Gilliam reported two earlier verbal conflicts between the boys the week of 9/7.

INFORMATION REVIEWED
- IEP and BIP. The BIP calls for check-in/check-out with Ms. Presley at 7:45 AM and a walk pass when he feels his "engine" rising.
- Staffing: the instructional aide who meets Ryder at the bus line was absent 9/10 through 9/15. No substitute was assigned to the morning check-in.
- Behavior data, 2026-27: 3 minor referrals (tardy, phone, profanity); 0 physical aggression before 9/15. On-task 71% of intervals in Algebra I.
- Re-evaluation data: Conners-4 Parent Hyperactivity/Impulsivity T = 81; Teacher T = 76. BASC-3 SRP Anxiety T = 69 (At-Risk). WISC-V FSIQ 97.
- Medical: ADHD diagnosed in 2020 by Dr. Imran Siddiqui, Sabra Pediatric & Family Medicine; Vyvanse 40 mg each morning. Mother reports he missed his dose that day because the refill was late.
- Outside counseling: Dustin Pelphrey, LCSW, Hilltop Family Counseling, weekly since his mamaw passed in May.
- Student statement: "I didn't think. He kept on about Dad and I just went." R.K.E. said he ran "so I wouldn't do nothing worse."

PARENT INPUT
Mrs. Kilgore said Ryder has been "wound tight" since his father, Jeremy Estep, was arrested in 2023, and worse since Mamaw Verna died. He spends weekends with his uncle Boyd Kilgore, helping at Kilgore's Garage & Wrecker and running trotlines. He is the only freshman on the NKHS bass fishing team and made the boat for the Oct. 10 tournament. Ms. Thacker asked that fishing not be taken away as a consequence. His uncle and the team call him "Tank." Mrs. Kilgore works days for Trinity Home Health and asked for calls after 4:00. The family attends Pawpaw Branch Church of God.

MANIFESTATION QUESTIONS
1. Was the conduct caused by, or did it have a direct and substantial relationship to, the child's disability?   [X] YES   [ ] NO
   Basis: an impulsive physical response to peer provocation is consistent with documented ADHD impulsivity (Conners-4 T = 81) and with the FBA hypothesis (peer provocation during unstructured transitions).
2. Was the conduct the direct result of the LEA's failure to implement the IEP?   [X] YES   [ ] NO
   Basis: the BIP morning check-in was not carried out 9/10 through 9/15.
DETERMINATION: The behavior WAS a manifestation of the disability. Team agreement: unanimous.

REQUIRED ACTIONS (34 CFR 300.530(f))
1. Ryder returns to his current placement on 9/28/26. The expulsion recommendation is withdrawn; days served count toward the 10 consecutive school days.
2. Review the FBA and revise the BIP within 15 school days. Dr. Belcher and Ms. Presley will collect ABC data in the bus line and cafeteria.
3. Add SDI Behavior/Social-Emotional, 20 min/day x 5 days (resource), including a coping plan for provocation.
4. A trained adult will staff the bus line check-in daily; named backup: Mr. Kirby.
5. Draft goal: When provoked by a peer, Ryder will use his walk pass or tell an adult within 1 minute in 4 of 5 opportunities, measured by staff log over 6 weeks.
6. Draft goal: Ryder will earn 80% of daily check-in/check-out points on 3 of 5 days per week.
7. Safety plan: separate seat assignments on Bus 31; driver informed.
8. Procedural Safeguards provided; parent informed of the right to appeal under 34 CFR 300.532.

NEXT MEETING: BIP review ARC, Oct. 13, 2026, 3:15 PM

text:
HIGHLAND RIVERS EDUCATIONAL COOPERATIVE (HREC)
ITINERANT DEAF/HARD OF HEARING SERVICES - ANNUAL SERVICES REPORT

STUDENT: STACY, GRACE L.            DOB: 08-21-2017      Age: 9      Grade: 3
Student ID: 3301987725              Medicaid ID: 5521009843
School: Otter Creek Elementary (OCE); teacher Mrs. Deanna Lykins, 3rd grade

Mailing: RR 4 Box 309-B, Garnet, KY 41630
Home: 555-0115     Mother cell: 606-555-0152     autumn.stacy@example.com
Itinerant teacher: Marisa Kincer, M.Ed., TOD/HH    606-555-0107 ext. 41    mkincer@hrec.example.org

BACKGROUND
Grace Lorraine Stacy failed her newborn hearing screen in 2017 and was diagnosed at 7 months with bilateral sensorineural hearing loss related to enlarged vestibular aqueducts (EVA). She was fit with hearing aids at age 1 and has had itinerant DHH services since preschool. Her loss is progressive: a drop in the left ear was measured after a fall from the trampoline in February 2024, and she was refit that spring. Children with EVA are advised to avoid head impacts, so Grace does not play Otter Creek youth soccer with her cousins. Gracie lives with Mamaw Juanita up Otter Creek, on the gravel lane past the Otter Creek Missionary Baptist Church, where she sits on the front pew so she can see the preacher's face. Her mother works evenings at Conley's Market in Garnet. Her father, Justin Stacy, works away on a pipeline crew in Texas and video-calls on Sundays with captions on.

AUDIOLOGICAL SUMMARY
Most recent audiogram 7/28/26: Dr. Lyle Burkhart, Au.D., Tri-County Hearing & Balance, (606) 555-0183, Acct. No. TCH-20914. ENT: Dr. Faisal Rahimi, Garnet Ear, Nose & Throat.
                               RIGHT              LEFT
Pure-tone average (PTA)        48 dB HL           61 dB HL
Speech Recognition Threshold   45 dB HL           60 dB HL
Word Recognition (quiet)       84% at 75 dB HL    68% at 85 dB HL
Aided SII                      0.71               0.52
Degree: moderate (R), moderately-severe (L), sloping configuration.
Devices: Phonak Sky Marvel behind-the-ear aids (S/N L 2219XK4470, R 2219XK4471) with Roger Touchscreen Mic and Roger receivers. School-owned Roger equipment tag PCS-AT-0087.

FUNCTIONAL LISTENING
- Functional Listening Evaluation (FLE), classroom, 9/10: quiet/close 92%; quiet/far 80%; noise/close 64%; noise/far 48%. With the Roger mic in noise/far: 88%.
- LIFE-R Teacher Appraisal (Mrs. Lykins): 62% - moderate listening difficulty, mostly in the cafeteria, the gym, and when peers answer.
- SIFTER: Academics PASS; Attention MARGINAL; Communication FAIL; Class Participation MARGINAL; School Behavior PASS.
- Ling Six Sound Check: 6/6 at 3 feet aided; misses /sh/ and /s/ at 9 feet with the left aid only.
- Speech intelligibility (Kenzie Lucas, CCC-SLP): 91% to unfamiliar listeners; /s/ blends distorted.

ACADEMIC IMPACT
Grace is reading at a 3rd-grade level (i-Ready Reading 519, on level), but vocabulary lags: PPVT-5 standard score 84 (14th percentile). Math is on grade level when word problems are read with the Roger mic on. Without the pass-around mic she misses about 1/3 of peer comments in whole-group discussion.

SERVICES PROVIDED (2025-2026)
Direct itinerant DHH instruction      30 minutes per week    self-advocacy, vocabulary, equipment
Consultation with classroom teacher   15 minutes per month
Equipment checks (34 CFR 300.113)     daily by aide; weekly by TOD
Grace received 31 of 34 scheduled sessions (3 missed for ENT appointments and a snow day).

DAILY LISTENING CHECK LOG - week of 9/21 (aide: Paulette Tipton)
Day    Aids on   Roger   Ling 6         Battery        Init.
Mon    Y         Y       6/6            OK             PT
Tue    Y         N*      6/6            R low          PT
Wed    Y         Y       5/6 (/sh/)     R replaced     PT
Thu    -- absent (ear infection) --
Fri    Y         Y       6/6            OK             GS (self-check with prompt)
*Roger charger left at Mamaw's; Mrs. Stacy brought it at noon.

SELF-ADVOCACY PROGRESS
Goal: Grace will tell an adult when a device is not working within 5 minutes in 4 of 5 opportunities. Baseline 1 of 5; current 3 of 5.
Goal: Grace will ask for repetition or clarification with a taught phrase in 80% of observed breakdowns. Current 55%.
On 9/10 Grace chose to present "My Ears" to her class and brought a photo of her pony, Dolly, wearing a toy hearing aid. She is the only student at OCE who wears hearing aids.

RECOMMENDATIONS FOR ARC (annual review 11/18/2026)
1. Continue Hearing Impairment eligibility; increase direct DHH service to 45 minutes per week for vocabulary.
2. Preferential seating near the teacher and away from the HVAC unit; pass-around mic for group talk.
3. Captions on all videos; written directions for multi-step tasks.
4. Train the new Bus 12 driver and cafeteria staff on the Roger mic.
5. Request an audiology re-check if the daily Ling check changes 2 days in a row.

PRESENT LEVELS OF ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENT AND FUNCTIONAL PERFORMANCE
Asher Lane Blankenship is an 8th grader who was diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder in spring 2017 by Dr. Kwame Osei at Weller Developmental Pediatrics. Asher ("Ash" at home) is a strong reader and a precise, literal thinker. He wears noise-canceling headphones in the hallway. Mr. Donnie Whitlock, instructional aide, meets him at the bus and walks the 8th-grade hall with him between classes. On Mondays and Thursdays he eats lunch in the science lab with two peers in the Lunch Bunch group led by Mr. Newsome; Mrs. Justice approved the space.

Communication: Mr. Brandon Akers, CCC-SLP, reports that Asher initiates with peers in 1 of 5 structured opportunities and rarely asks follow-up questions; he answers in long monologues about weather. He repairs a breakdown when cued visually 60% of the time.

3. Written expression: Given a graphic organizer, Asher will write a 3-paragraph response with a topic sentence and at least 2 transitions per paragraph, scoring 3 of 4 on the district rubric in 4 of 5 samples.

DIAGNOSIS AND HISTORY
Skylar Dawn Fyffe ("Sky") has epilepsy (childhood absence epilepsy with generalized tonic-clonic seizures), diagnosed in April 2024 after her first convulsive seizure during the Sunday service at Mossy Bottom Church of Christ. She had no convulsive seizures over the summer.
Neurologist: Dr. Victor Almeida, Hawthorne Children's Neurology Clinic, (304) 555-0117, MRN HCN-0093318.
Primary care: Dr. Glenda Rakes, Mossy Bottom Family Medicine, 606-555-0124.

SEIZURE TYPES
Absence: stares 10-15 seconds, eyelids flutter, stops talking; up to 20 per day when tired or sick. Rescue medication is not needed.
Generalized tonic-clonic: stiffening, then jerking of arms and legs; may cry out; usually lasts 1-2 minutes; sleepy and confused for 30-60 minutes (post-ictal).
Triggers: missed sleep, fever, missed medication, flashing lights.

SEIZURE ACTION PLAN - STAY, SAFE, SIDE
1. STAY with her, stay calm, and TIME the seizure. Note the start time.
2. Keep her SAFE: move furniture, cushion her head, nothing in her mouth.
3. Turn her on her SIDE once the jerking slows.
4. Give Valtoco 10 mg in one nostril if a convulsive seizure lasts 5 minutes or longer, OR for a cluster of 3 or more seizures in 1 hour.
5. CALL 911 if Valtoco is given, if breathing is difficult after the seizure, or if the seizure happens in water. Then call the parent.
6. Record on the seizure log and notify the school nurse.
Water safety: no swimming without a 1:1 adult within arm's reach.
